attrs.evidence: lowering.mjs 0.2.0 freezes INPUT_PORT_SPEC, INSTANTIATION_SPEC, INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID, inputsSemId, portSemId and INSTANTIATION_RECEIPT_FIELDS, with instantiate() throwing instantiate-not-implemented. LOWERING_SEM_ID MOVED as a consequence and that is the point: LOWERING_SPEC carries inputs_model, so deciding the model changes the lowering relation, and an id that survived the ruling unchanged would be claiming the decision was not part of the relation. lowering_check.mjs case 'out-of-fragment-refused' asserts decided true, implemented false, three DECLARED falsifiers, and INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID distinct from LOWERING_SEM_ID; 9/9 with the refinement witness unchanged and still FILM-EVIDENCED. THE THREE FALSIFIERS ARE DECLARED AND NONE IS WRITTEN -- I-4a allocation-invariance, I-4b source-name-sensitivity, I-4c binding-has-force -- so this law is PROPERTY-TESTED for the DECISION and its refusal surface, and carries NO claim about instantiation behaviour, which does not exist yet. B2 writes the three. B1.1: lowering_check.mjs case 'semantic-ids-track-semantics-only' asserts that no lifecycle field appears in either semantic projection AND that the projections remain sensitive -- dropping `add` from lowered_ops moves the LOWERING id while changing extra-input semantics or making the source name non-semantic moves the INSTANTIATION id and not lowering's, which is the two-relation ruling measured rather than asserted. Case 'extra-inputs-ignored-by-the-source' runs the real evaluator: input(x) with {x:2, y:999} returns 2, with {} raises program-input-missing. 11/11, and the refinement witness is unchanged and still FILM-EVIDENCED. B1.2: lowering_check.mjs case 'target-template-is-the-pre-allocation-layer' shows the codomain is {t:add,a:{t:church,n:2},b:{t:church,n:3}} with no names and no labels, that emit() reproduces the SAME 129 characters of ic32 the pre-template lowering produced -- so introducing the layer changed neither the executable term nor its outcome -- that a template holding a port is emit-unbound-port rather than emitted, and that structural equality is identity while add(3,2) differs. 12/12, refinement unchanged and still FILM-EVIDENCED. B1.2.1: lowering.mjs 0.5.0 adds TARGET_EXECUTABLE_ENCODING_SEM_ID, names it as INSTANTIATION_SEMANTICS.codomain_encoding_sem_id, removes the leftover target_encoding binding from LOWERING_SEMANTICS, adds op_lowering_rules, uncrosses the two refusal vocabularies and keeps the B1.2 ids as SUPERSEDED_CODOMAIN_SEM_IDS. Measured by lowering_check emit-is-not-a-hidden-relation. STILL DECLARED, NOT BUILT: instantiate() throws and the three port falsifiers remain DECLARED -- B1.2.1 changed no behaviour.
attrs.revision_note: SUPERSEDED at B2, when the relation it describes became EXECUTABLE, and kept as history. Revision 3 described a decided-and-unbuilt architecture; nothing in it was false and no verdict rested on behaviour that did not exist -- instantiate() had never run. What changed is that the claims are now witnessed rather than declared.
attrs.statement: INSTANTIATION IS A SEPARATE RELATION FROM LOWERING AND CARRIES ITS OWN IDENTITY. A target template can be perfectly lowered while instantiation binds "x" to the port for "y". Merge the two relations and a target failure becomes ambiguous between A MISTRANSLATED PROGRAM and CORRECTLY TRANSLATED CODE WITH MISWIRED INPUTS, which is the class of ambiguity this record has spent twenty-seven rounds removing. So: program_sem_id -(lowering_sem_id)-> target_template_sem_id, reusable and independent of invocation data; then target_template_sem_id + inputs_sem_id -(instantiation_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, the closed executable term. The earlier framing, PARAMETERIZED versus INSTANTIATED, was a FALSE CHOICE: the template is parameterized AND the executed term is necessarily closed. instantiation_sem_id IDENTIFIES THE RELATION AND NOT THE INVOCATION -- it commits to the input-port namespace and version, the source-name-to-port rule, missing- and extra-input semantics, the canonical embedding of an input value, template substitution semantics, the refusal vocabulary and the conformance vectors, and it does NOT contain x=5, which is inputs_sem_id. THE PORT IS BOUND TO THE SOURCE NAME: port identity is H(namespace | canonicalBytes(source_input_name)), taken at the canonical target-AST layer as {op:"input-port", source_name:N} BEFORE any textual or ic32 variable allocation, so two implementations that internally allocate _impl17 and q93 reach the SAME target_template_sem_id. The quotient is exact and it is the INVERSE OF ROUND 16: internal target variable names are non-semantic and alpha-equivalent, source input keys are semantic. Round 16's bug was identity depending on a spelling that should not matter; the danger here is identity depending on an ALLOCATION that should not matter while losing the SOURCE NAME that must. SOURCE INPUT NAMES ARE NOT UNICODE-NORMALIZED: if the frozen core distinguishes two code-point sequences as different names, port identity preserves that exact distinction, because normalizing at the encoding layer is a language-semantic change made where the source cannot see it. INSTANTIATION GETS NO FILM -- it is a deterministic relation, not a transition system, so its instrument is independent RE-INSTANTIATION against an InstantiationReceipt {target_template_sem_id, instantiation_sem_id, inputs_sem_id, target_term_sem_id}, the same argument that gives lowering re-lowering. DECIDED, NOT BUILT, and the two states are distinguishable by name: `input` refuses as lower-input-not-implemented rather than lower-inputs-undecided, because a refusal that conflates 'we have not ruled' with 'we have ruled and not written it' is a stale instrument with a delay fuse. CORRECTED AT B1.1, TWICE, AND BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE PART OF THE LAW. (1) A SEMANTIC IDENTITY MAY NOT HASH LIFECYCLE. B1's first cut hashed the whole spec, so flipping `implemented` from false to true moved LOWERING_SEM_ID from lsem-5673108765b4 to lsem-63f98923ed13 without one rule changing, and rewording the conformance-test STATUS sentence moved INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID. B2 becoming BUILT would therefore have re-identified a relation B1 froze -- round 16's defect arriving inside the compiler specification. The split is SEMANTICS (what the relation does; changing it changes emitted terms or accepted inputs) versus STATUS (rounds, evidence grades, whether code exists), and only the first is hashed, under new TRVM-*-SEM-v2 domain tags. The overbound B1 ids are KEPT as OVERBOUND_TRANSITIONAL_SEM_IDS rather than erased. DECLARED OPEN and not solved: the semantic records are still English, and rewording normative prose such as dup_label_policy or substitution still moves an id; a formal target-AST grammar would close that and is not written. (2) EXTRA CANONICAL INPUTS ARE IGNORED, NOT REFUSED, AND THE ORIGINAL ARGUMENT WAS FALSE. B1 froze extra inputs as instantiate-extra-input on the reasoning that accepting them would let inputs_sem_id vary while target_term_sem_id did not, 'so the receipt would stop being a function'. A function may be many-to-one; (template, {x:2}) and (template, {x:2, unused:999}) mapping to one term IS a function. Worse, the rule contradicted the source: evaluate({op:'input',name:'x'}, {}, {x:2, y:999}) returns 2, so refusing extras at the target would have broken refinement BY CONSTRUCTION on the first program carrying a spare input. Different inputs_sem_id mapping to the same target_term_sem_id is the correct statement that executable semantics do not depend on unused data. Narrowing the source's input discipline is a SOURCE-LANGUAGE change requiring a new CORE_SEM_ID, and the instantiator may not impose it unilaterally. THE REFINEMENT CLAIM IS SCOPED BEFORE IT IS MADE: it holds over canonical, fully bound input environments in which instantiation succeeds. Missing inputs are refused on BOTH sides but at different layers under different codes -- program-input-missing during source evaluation, instantiate-missing-input before any target term exists -- so SOURCE-REFUSAL to INSTANTIATION-REFUSAL preservation is a separate theorem and is DECLARED OPEN. AND I-4c MANDATES AN ASYMMETRIC FIXTURE: add(input(x), input(y)) with x=2,y=3 gives 5 under the correct binding and 5 under the swap, so the obvious witness is green whether or not the binding was honoured. The mandated fixture is add(input(x), add(input(x), input(y))) with x=2,y=3, which gives 7 correctly and 8 swapped. COMPLETED AT B1.2, because @2 froze an architecture the compiler could not express. lower() emitted an ic32 STRING, so there was no canonical target-AST layer for {op:'input-port'} to live at and a port could only have become a placeholder like $input_x -- spelling as semantics, the very defect this law forbids, reintroduced by the absence of the representation it presumes. THE CODOMAIN OF LOWERING IS A TEMPLATE: TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1, grammar church(n) | add(Template, Template) | port(source_name), with its own content-bound encoding identity. A TEMPLATE CONTAINS NO BINDER NAMES AND NO DUP LABELS -- emit() invents both from the template's shape by the declared depth-first policy -- so I-4a is a property of the DATA STRUCTURE and not a convention an emitter is asked to respect: there is no field an allocation could occupy. emit() REFUSES a template still holding a port (emit-unbound-port), because a template with a free port is not an executable term. The LoweringReceipt therefore ends at target_template_sem_id, not target_term_sem_id; a receipt ending at the term keeps asserting that lowering produced the executable term, which this law denies. AND THE HASHED SEMANTICS NOW CARRY THE WHOLE SOURCE FRAGMENT INCLUDING `input`: @2 left it out of lowered_ops, so B2 adding it would have moved LOWERING_SEM_ID -- implementing a frozen rule re-identifying the relation, which is exactly what the B1.1 correction set out to prevent. The rule is frozen ({op:'input',name:N} lowers to {t:'port',source_name:N}, N carried through unchanged) and the implementation is absent, and lower-input-not-implemented is a STATUS refusal that is deliberately NOT in refusal_semantics. Measured: implementing the input rule AND flipping both lifecycle flags moves neither semantic id. CORRECTED AT B1.2.1, AND emit() WAS A HIDDEN SEMANTIC RELATION. B1.2 moved lowering's codomain onto the template and left BOTH encoding commitments pointing where they had pointed when there was no template. MEASURED: change the add combinator and nothing else, and the executable term's bytes change while INSTANTIATION_SEM_ID, target_template_sem_id and the template-encoding id all stand still -- so the identity of the relation that PRODUCES those bytes did not move. LOWERING_SEM_ID moved instead, which is the same mistake facing the other way. UNDER-BOUND: INSTANTIATION_SEMANTICS named its codomain in PROSE, 'TRVM-TERM-CANON-v1 / ic32 executable text, via emit()', so the whole executable encoding reached the relation's identity only as a symbol name inside an English sentence -- a label anyone may claim, the objection the primitive ruling already raised against a bare componentReachability. OVER-BOUND: LOWERING_SEMANTICS still carried the entire TARGET_ENCODING, a pre-template leftover of the same class as the LoweringReceipt that kept ending at target_term_sem_id, which B1.2 fixed one declaration away and missed here; an emitter change therefore re-identified every LoweringReceipt ever issued, for a relation lowering does not perform. THE RULE: A RELATION'S IDENTITY MUST COMMIT, BY CONTENT AND NOT BY NAME, TO EXACTLY THE ENCODINGS OF ITS OWN DOMAIN AND CODOMAIN -- no more and no fewer. Lowering commits to TRVM-TARGET-TEMPLATE-v1 and to its own per-op map; instantiation commits to the template encoding as domain and to TARGET_EXECUTABLE_ENCODING_SEM_ID as codomain, and EMISSION IS INSIDE THE INSTANTIATION RELATION. That last is a ruling with a stated trigger for revisiting it rather than a convenience: a third relation with its own emission_sem_id is the more faithful decomposition, because a correct port substitution can coexist with an incorrect emitter, and it is NOT taken while emit() is neither independently reused nor independently theorem-bearing. MEASURED IN THREE DIRECTIONS: an emitter change moves the instantiation id ALONE, a per-op lowering-rule change moves lowering's ALONE, and a template-grammar change moves BOTH because it is the boundary they share. REMOVING THE LEFTOVER BINDING EXPOSED A SECOND GAP: nothing in the hashed lowering semantics said that a const becomes a church node or that add's operand order is preserved -- B1.1 froze the `input` rule and const and add were left implicit -- so const(n) lowering to church(n+1) would have contradicted no sentence. An identity that cannot move when its map changes is the same defect as one that moves when its map has not. AND THE REFUSAL VOCABULARIES WERE CROSSED: the executable encoding listed four lower-* source-fragment refusals that cannot arise while emitting, while lowering claimed emit-unbound-port and template-malformed, neither reachable from lower(), which emits only zero-port templates it built itself. Each list now belongs to the record that owns it, and every name lowering claims is driven to a refusal by the witness.
